extraction.name: SWE-Gym
extraction.description: An environment for training software engineering agents and verifiers. It contains 2,438 real-world Python task instances with executable runtime environments, unit tests, and natural-language task descriptions.
extraction.creator: Jiayi Pan, Xingyao Wang, Graham Neubig, Navdeep Jaitly, Heng Ji, Alane Suhr, Yizhe Zhang
extraction.publisher: Proceedings of the 42nd International Conference on Machine Learning (PMLR 267, 2025)
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The authors identified Python repositories using SEART GitHub search, filtering for repositories created before July 1, 2022 with more than 500 stars, at least 300 lines of code, more than 500 pull requests, and 100 contributors. They then used SWE-Bench’s instance extraction script to convert these repositories into task instances from pull requests, and expert-validated test cases were added.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Pull requests from 11 popular Python repositories on GitHub, converted into software engineering task instances; the dataset comprises 2,438 real-world tasks.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Approximately 200 human annotation hours were used to manually configure dependencies for each task instance using repository configuration files, CI scripts, or documentation, and then SWE-Bench’s execution-based validation script was used to ensure the gold patch passed more unit tests than the original code. The paper also notes that annotations were done by a subset of the authors.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Instances were validated using SWE-Bench’s execution-based validation script; failed instances were filtered out after validation.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: SWE-Bench’s execution-based validation script was used to validate instances; no other machine annotation tools are described.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset may have distribution bias if executable environments are ignored, and its task distribution is long-tailed across repositories, with some repositories dominating the data.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: SWE-Gym is limited to Python tasks from 11 repositories, and performance may be affected by repository selection and task difficulty. The paper also notes that SWE-Gym Lite excludes harder or more complex tasks, and that SWE-Gym Raw lacks executable environments and validated tests. The authors further state that performance is currently limited by compute budget rather than dataset size.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is intended to accelerate research on software engineering agents and verifiers, potentially improving automation of GitHub issue resolution and software development workflows.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training software engineering agents and verifiers, including fine-tuning language models on agent-environment interaction trajectories and training verifier models for inference-time scaling. SWE-Gym Lite is positioned for rapid prototyping and evaluation.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The paper publicly releases SWE-Gym, SWE-Gym Raw, SWE-Gym Lite, models, agent trajectories, and pre-built Docker images for reproducibility. No explicit update cadence, maintainer plan, or deprecation policy is stated.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: SWE-Gym Lite was created by following the SWE-Bench Lite filtering pipeline and excluding tasks that require editing more than one file, tasks with poorly described problem statements, those with excessively complex ground-truth code diffs, and tests focused on error message validation.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Repositories were filtered using SEART GitHub search to select Python repositories created before July 1, 2022 with more than 500 stars, at least 300 lines of code, more than 500 pull requests, and 100 contributors; instances were extracted with SWE-Bench’s script; versions were semi-automatically collected from repository information; dependencies were manually configured using requirements files, CI scripts, or documentation; and instances were validated with SWE-Bench’s execution-based validation script, filtering out failed instances.

name.evidence: We present SWE-Gym, the first environment for training software engineering (SWE) agents.

description.evidence: SWE-Gym contains 2,438 real-world task instances, each comprising a Python codebase with an executable runtime environment, unit tests, and a task specified in natural language.
